We have another use case for this: a RAG evidence gate sharing a backbone with a generative model.

We've published the [serving plugin](https://github.com/ThakiCloud/ecp-shared-backbone-vllm) and [weights](https://huggingface.co/ThakiCloud/ECP-SB-27B-Research). events.body:
Two follow-ups to the RFC, measured with the draft PRs (#63897, #63898, #63899) and the Connex plugin on 4x A40 (PCIe, no NVLink) + 100 Gb InfiniBand, Llama-3-8B:

1. **Transport cost.** With same-host hops over CUDA IPC (the GPU sets and waits on flags itself, `cuStreamWaitValue32`/`cuStreamWriteValue32`, no Python on the data path) and RDMA between hosts, end-to-end TPOT is within run-to-run noise of vLLM's NCCL path for PP=2, PP=4 and PP=2 x TP=2 on one host (3 runs per cell), and 2-3% higher at C=1 across two hosts. Per hop on one host a 32 MB step takes 0.80 ms vs 1.54 ms for vLLM's NCCL path (which also pays ~0.4 ms per hop for its gloo metadata); small messages are noisier in the plugin. So the "PP does not need NCCL" premise holds without a throughput cost here.

2. **What failover buys.** Same load (32 streaming clients), SIGKILL of a stage-1 process, 3 kills each: stock vLLM PP…

Follow-up with fixes (all in the plugin, no change to the PRs):

- PP=2 x TP=2 failover now works, including a stage restarted in place without a spare (32/32 in-flight requests completed in 3 kills; stock vLLM with a restart loop loses all and is down ~60 s). The bug was the plugin launching steps while a stage had no live replica.
- A design point for anyone implementing a non-NCCL PP group: a CUDA stream wait that a Python thread of the same process releases deadlocks against CUDA calls that hold the GIL and wait for the device (a first Triton kernel load, which a freshly started replica does in its first steps). It did hang a cross-host failover here. On one host the plugin avoids it by having the sender's GPU set the receiver's flag (CUDA IPC + `cuStreamWriteValue32`); across hosts it now waits on the CPU, which costs ~5 ms per token at PP=2, C=1 (34.2 vs 28.9 ms; NCCL 28.3 ms).
